t: You're at Eaton Square in Belgravia, the largest square in London. It was built by the Grosvenor family and named after their Cheshire country house, Eaton Hall. Thomas Cubitt laid out the first block from 1827. It's larger but less grand than Belgrave Square. Many of the town houses are now upmarket apartments. Several well-known people have a link with the square. The actress Vivien Leigh died here. So did the colonial administrator Charles Trevelyan, the bishop and poet Richard Chenevix Trench, and Ruth Roche, Baroness Fermoy, grandmother of Diana, Princess of Wales.
